description: Extends the org preset `local>Heey-Global/.github`, which supplies `config:recommended`, the `h-teske` assignment, the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge` and the 0-day fast-track for vulnerability alerts. Those four are therefore NOT repeated here; before 2026-09 this repository extended `config:recommended` directly and set `assignees` locally, which meant it silently ran with NO stability window at all while rules below already described the org policy as applying. The `.npmrc` at the repository root carries the same 3-day floor for manual `npm install`, so both update paths share one number. `ignoreNpmrcFile` keeps that floor out of Renovate's own lockfile updates: npm would otherwise apply it while resolving, which would silently override the preset's `vulnerabilityAlerts.minimumReleaseAge: 0 days` and block exactly the security bumps the fast-track exists for. Nothing else lives in that `.npmrc` — registry auth comes from Renovate's host rules — so ignoring it costs nothing.

Digest cooldown gap, deliberate: the org preset exempts `digest`/`pinDigest` updates from `minimumReleaseAge` because digests carry no datasource timestamp, and re-imposes the soak through the org `digest-age` required workflow. That workflow rule is NOT among the org rules applied to this repository's `main` (only `gitleaks.yml` is), so digest updates here land without a soak — unchanged from before this repository extended the preset, but no longer covered by the preset's own coupling argument. Closing it means adding `digest-age-check.yml` to the org ruleset for this repository, not editing this file: re-imposing `minimumReleaseAge` on digests locally would park every digest PR on `renovate/stability-days` forever, which is the failure the exemption exists to avoid.

Schedules are evaluated in Europe/Berlin (`:timezone`). Without that preset Renovate uses UTC, so the previous `before 6am on monday` actually fired until 08:00 local — inside working hours. The nightly 01:00-06:00 window applies to branch creation AND rebases: since ci.yml moved onto the self-hosted runners (2026-07-12) every Renovate push competes with interactive work for the same four runners, so keeping those pushes out of the day is what protects CI latency. `rebaseWhen: conflicted` replaces the `auto` default, which rebased every open PR on each push to main and re-ran the full matrix per rebase.

packageRules.description: Group all @types/* type-definition devDependencies into one PR. They are type-only, so a bad bump fails typecheck (never runtime); batching them avoids a separate full CI matrix per @types package.
Group lint/format/type tooling into a single PR

First-party Verity images - immediate PRs, deliberately exempt from the repo-wide nightly window. Only external dependencies are batched into 01:00-06:00; project images are published continuously and must be picked up the same day.

Keep the Verity repository devcontainer on the moving verity-sandbox tag. This repository is the integration consumer for the fleet image; digest-pinning its Dockerfile ARG would silently detach it from toolkit and base-image releases that every other project receives. Deployment images and GitHub Actions remain covered by the repo-wide docker:pinDigests preset.

Type the website's base-image bumps `fix` rather than the `chore` a Docker dependency otherwise gets. The Verity website has its own release-please train (`website-vX.Y.Z`), and the cluster pins that version — a `chore(deps)` nginx bump would land on main, publish a `sha-<commit>` image, and never produce a released version for the k8s pin to move to, so the deployed site would keep serving the old base image until something unrelated happened to release the website. `fix` makes the security bump its own patch release, which is what it is.

The agent CLIs (claude-code, codex, opencode, pi) and their ACP transport adapters ship ~daily. Group patch/minor bumps into ONE PR instead of a PR per release. Merge is MANUAL and the org preset's 3-day `minimumReleaseAge` applies (since 2026-09 it actually does — see the top-level description) — this rule deliberately sets no `automerge`. It previously carried `schedule: ["at any time"]` to escape the repo-wide WEEKLY Monday schedule and keep these ~daily releases on their own cadence (ADR 0004 D1). The repo-wide schedule is now nightly-daily, so that intent is satisfied without an override: the daily cadence is preserved, the PR just appears overnight instead of mid-workday. The explicit window is kept here so the ADR-0004-D1 intent stays visible at the rule. Runtime self-update is disabled in the Feature (updates arrive via image rebuild / Feature republish), so these pins are the single version channel. For each tool the install.sh shell-default pin and the Feature-manifest default share the depName, so both bump in lock-step within the one branch. Majors fall through to a normal, visible PR for manual review.

Never bump React independently. `react`, `react-dom`, and `react-test-renderer` (apps/mobile) are dictated by the Expo SDK / react-native version: React must EXACTLY match react-native's embedded `react-native-renderer` (NOT a separate npm package) or the app crashes at boot with 'Incompatible React versions'. PR #723 did exactly this — bumped react to 19.2.7 while RN 0.85.3 ships renderer 19.2.3. These move ONLY when the Expo SDK / react-native is bumped (via `expo install`), never on their own.

customManagers.description: Track globally-installed CLIs pinned via `RUN npm install -g pkg@ver` in the deploy Dockerfiles — the stock dockerfile manager only parses FROM/ARG image lines, not RUN, so without this the pin silently freezes. Covers deploy/Dockerfile (Server image) and deploy/verity-sandbox.Dockerfile (Sandbox base).

Track version pins declared as shell `VAR="${OVERRIDE:-VERSION}"` in features/verity-sandbox-toolkit/install.sh (the single source of truth for the gh/doppler/claude-code/codex/opencode/pi versions). The stock managers don't parse shell-default expansions, so without this the annotated pins silently freeze. The captured value is the literal default after `:-`.

Track the version DEFAULTS in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest so the CLI pins stay in lock-step with install.sh. Matches the JSON `"<opt>Version": { ... "default": "<ver>" }` blocks; the depName is mapped per option id below.
Track the claudeAcpVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp pin.
Track the codexVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's @openai/codex pin.
Track the codexAcpVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp pin.
Track the opencodeVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's opencode-ai pin.
Track the piVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent pin.

Track the ghVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest (cli/cli). No extractVersion: the pin form is bare `2.95.0` and Renovate's semver versioning strips the release tag's leading `v` on compare — matches install.sh's manager + the dev-server precedent, so both cli/cli managers bump in lock-step.
Track the dopplerVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest (DopplerHQ/cli).

Track the gitleaksVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest (gitleaks/gitleaks), in lock-step with install.sh's gitleaks pin. Same bare-version form as the cli/cli manager: releases are tagged v<version> and Renovate's semver versioning strips the leading v on compare.
